battle.name: 上加拿大叛亂
battle.theater: 約克城與尼亞加拉河沿岸
battle.brief: 一八三七年十二月，改革派在約克城起事。麥肯齊率叛軍在蒙特哥馬利酒館與政府軍交火，砲彈打進酒館飯廳窗戶，叛軍當場潰散。首領退入美國，於尼亞加拉河的海軍島宣布加拿大共和國，翌年一月被英軍逐出，戰事轉為跨境襲擊，直至一八三八年十二月溫莎之役才被平定。野砲是這一役唯一見於記載的火炮。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 上加拿大叛亂的交戰雙方，一方是英屬上加拿大的殖民政府及其武裝，另一方是改革派組成的武裝與後來捲入的美國獵手小屋會。英方包括：駐紮金安大略的英國正規軍分遣隊，由上校查爾斯·戈爾與陸軍中校麥克斯米利安·格洛本斯基分節；約克（今多倫多）城與周邊的上加拿大民兵團、城市守備義勇與省政府的警務人員；另有從下加拿大戰區抽調、新近開到的第83步兵團這樣的部隊，以及皇家海軍的艦隊武裝與登陸艇隊，支援品是從英國運來的野砲與火藥。總督弗朗西斯·邦德·海德是英方的政治核心，他倚重「家庭公約」的官僚集團與一八三六年由奧蘭治會社支持的保王派，主持了議會選舉、拒絕撥款、撤回赦免條件，最後下令由菲茨吉本率民兵出擊。叛方沒有正式建制：一八三七年改革派在多倫多組成政治聯盟與警醒委員會，許多地方的農民、獵人與鐵匠按村落自組隊伍，武器多為獵槍與舊式步槍，另在城北鍛造長矛；首領威廉·萊昂·麥肯齊是唯一貫穿全程的指揮者，塞繆爾·勞恩特、安東尼·范埃格蒙德、安東尼·安德森與彼得·馬修斯分掌武裝，彼得·馬修斯是從紐約回來的流亡者，一八三七年十月參與制憲會議。叛亂失敗後，美國境內的獵手小屋會接手，於一八三八年秋組織入侵，紐約州與聯邦政府一面默許、一面以違反中立法追究其首腦。
countriesEn: In the Upper Canada Rebellion the two sides were, on one hand, the colonial government of British Upper Canada and the forces it could raise, and on the other, the armed bands organised by the Reformers and, later, the American Hunters' Lodges drawn in from across the border. The British side comprised detachments of regular British troops stationed in the Kingston area, under the command of Colonel Charles Gore and Lieutenant-Colonel Maximilien Globensky; the militia regiments of Upper Canada with the city guards and volunteers of York, present-day Toronto, and the provincial constabulary; detachments such as the newly arrived 83rd Regiment of Foot sent down from the Lower Canada theatre; and the naval detachments and landing parties of the Royal Navy, supplied with field guns and ammunition shipped out from Britain. The political core of the British side was the Lieutenant Governor, Francis Bond Head, who relied on the Family Compact of officeholders and on the Tory candidates supported by the Orange Order in 1836, presided over the parliamentary elections, refused supply, withdrew the terms of amnesty, and finally ordered the militia out under FitzGibbon. The rebel side had no formal establishment. In 1837 the Reformers organised a Political Union and vigilance committees in Toronto; in many townships farmers, hunters and blacksmiths formed bands on their own initiative, armed chiefly with hunting rifles and old muskets, and pikes were forged north of the city. William Lyon Mackenzie was the only commander who ran the whole course of the revolt; Samuel Lount, Anthony Van Egmond, Anthony Anderson and Peter Matthews each commanded part of the fighting, Matthews being an exile returned from New York who had sat in the Constitutional Convention of October 1837. After the revolt failed, the Hunters' Lodges on the American side took over and staged an invasion in the autumn of 1838, while the state of New York and the federal government looked the other way and at the same time pursued the movement's leaders for violating the Neutrality Act.
people: 威廉·萊昂·麥肯齊是上加拿大叛亂的樞紐。他是報紙《 constitution 》的主編與改革派領袖，一八三六年在選舉中連同勞恩特一起落選後，於一八三七年組建多倫多政治聯盟，七月召開制憲會議，散發宣言與傳單，宣稱只要總督讓立法議會自行選出行政委員就會和平收場。他在十二月五日率領叛軍向約克城行軍，卻在路上被二十六名民兵的一輪射擊嚇退，次日再集結時又因意見分歧耽誤，最後由安東尼·范埃格蒙德說服眾人據守酒館，麥肯齊仍主張主動出擊。塞繆爾·勞恩特是叛軍最早的武裝首領，一八三七年十二月四日率隊進城，在揚奇街上與保王派騎兵遭遇，路障與槍戰中保王派上尉羅伯特·穆迪中彈身亡；安東尼·安德森被市議員約翰·鮑威爾擊中頸部重傷，麥肯齊遂在十二月的會議上被推為叛軍首領。詹姆斯·菲茨吉本原是英方最關鍵的人物：他在十一月就警告總督英軍將被抽調、要求武裝民兵，卻屢遭拒絕；叛亂爆發後他被任命為民兵副總司令並組成參謀部，是他把一千二百人與兩門砲的隊伍組織起來。殖民地總督海德表現反覆：他先提出全面赦免並讓羅爾夫與鮑德溫前往談判，聞知叛軍要求書面文件後又撤回條件，最終下令出擊。阿倫·麥克納布自漢密爾頓率六十人趕到，後來再赴倫敦鎮平定鄧科姆的起事。一八三七年十二月，麥肯齊、鄧科姆、羅爾夫與二百名支持者退入尼亞加拉河的海軍島宣布成立加拿大共和國；一八三八年一月十三日英軍進攻，島上守軍潰散，麥肯齊在美國本土被捕。一八三八年的獵手小屋會階段，芬蘭－瑞典出身的軍人尼爾斯·冯·舒爾茨率領攻擊普雷斯考特的風車堡，終在十一月十六日英軍炮兵自京斯頓赶到時崩潰；十二月四日溫莎之役中，第32步兵團的外科醫生約翰·休姆陣亡。
peopleEn: William Lyon Mackenzie was the pivot of the Upper Canada Rebellion. He was the proprietor of the newspaper The Constitution and the leading Reformer; after being defeated in the 1836 elections together with Lount he organised the Toronto Political Union in 1837, convened a Constitutional Convention in July, and printed declarations and broadsides arguing that the colony would settle itself peacefully as soon as the Lieutenant Governor allowed the assembly to elect the executive council. On 5 December he marched the rebels towards York, was scattered by a single volley from twenty-six militiamen on the road, and on the following day lost more time to argument until Anthony Van Egmond persuaded the men to hold the tavern while Mackenzie still wanted to attack. Samuel Lount was the first armed leader of the revolt; on 4 December 1837 he marched into the city and met the loyalist cavalry on Yonge Street, and in the fighting at the roadblock the loyalist captain Robert Moodie was shot and killed, while Anthony Anderson was mortally wounded in the neck by the alderman John Powell, after which the rebel leaders made Mackenzie their commander in a meeting that same month. James FitzGibbon was the most important man on the British side. He warned the Lieutenant Governor in November that the regulars were being stripped from the colony and asked for an armed militia, and was refused; once the revolt broke out he was appointed adjutant general of the militia, organised the staff, and was the man who assembled the column of twelve hundred men and two guns. The Lieutenant Governor, Head, was indecisive: he first offered a general amnesty and sent Rolph and Baldwin to negotiate, then withdrew the offer when he learned the rebels wanted it in writing, and finally ordered the attack. Allan MacNab brought sixty men in from Hamilton and later went to the London district to break Duncombe's rising. In December 1837 Mackenzie, Duncombe, Rolph and some two hundred supporters withdrew to Navy Island in the Niagara and proclaimed the Republic of Canada; on 13 January 1838 the British attacked, the garrison on the island broke, and Mackenzie was arrested on the American mainland. In the Hunters' Lodge phase of 1838, the Finnish-Swedish soldier Nils Szoltevsky von Schoultz led the attack on the battery at Windmill Hill near Prescott, and the attempt collapsed on 16 November when British artillery was brought up from Kingston; in the action at Windsor on 4 December the surgeon John Hume of the 32nd Foot was killed.
kits: 野砲在這場叛亂裡的位置很特殊：它不是大軍的戰具，而是兩門從省城約克調來的輕型野砲，卻決定了蒙特哥馬利酒館一役的勝負。一八三七年時上加拿大的炮兵編制極小，殖民地政府手中只有為數不多的野砲，銅或鐵質、幾磅到十幾磅口徑，安裝在輕型兩輪砲架上，砲身與砲架可以拆成幾件由一匹或兩匹馬拉走，因此能從多倫多沿著結冰的土路拉到城北；這正是野砲相對攻城砲的看家本領，拆得開、走得動、跟得上。叛軍這邊沒有同樣的火力：他們用獵槍、老式步槍、刀劍與城北鍛造來對付騎兵的長矛，第一線的射擊精度與射程都遠不如配定裝藥的軍用步槍，交戰往往靠距離與數量取勝。政府軍的兩門砲在十二月七日開進時做了關鍵的一件事：把砲口對準蒙特哥馬利酒館的飯廳窗戶直接平射，一發砲彈打穿窗板並在室內炸開，屋裡的叛軍當即崩潰；此後史家記錄的戰果也集中在這一發砲彈上，砲兵成了決定勝負的兵種，而不是步槍。武器之外，這場叛亂還牽動了其他裝備：英方的蒸汽輪船 United States、Charlotte of Toronto 與巡邏艇用於封鎖尼亞加拉河與聖勞倫斯河；一八三七年十一月十三日，愛國者一度奪下普雷斯考特風車堡的英軍砲台，一八三八年十一月再攻同一處時，自京斯頓趕來的英軍炮兵到場，包圍才告解除。英方在邊境上唯一成建制的重火力就是那座砲台與援軍砲兵。叛軍後來的攻擊則大量依賴汽船把越境者送上岸，一八三八年五月曾登船奪走英國汽船 Sir Robert Peel，這些船隻同時是他們跨越邊界的唯一手段與最脆弱的一環。
kitsEn: The field gun's place in this rebellion is peculiar. It was not an instrument of a great army but two light pieces brought down from the provincial capital of York, and they decided the battle at Montgomery's Tavern. The artillery establishment of Upper Canada in 1837 was minute: the colonial government held only a handful of field pieces, of brass or iron, from a few pounds up to a dozen or so, mounted on light two-wheeled carriages, with the barrel and carriage separable so that the pieces could be broken into parts and drawn by one horse or a pair. That was the field gun's virtue over a siege gun: it could be taken apart, moved and kept up with the column, and so the two guns came up the frozen dirt road from Toronto to the north of the city. The rebels had no equivalent firepower. They used hunting rifles, old muskets, swords and pikes forged north of the city to meet cavalry, and the accuracy and range of their musketry fell well short of service muskets using paper cartridges, so their fire fights were decided by range and numbers. The two guns did one decisive thing when they came in on 7 December: they were laid on the dining-room window of the Montgomery's Tavern and fired level into it, a single round passing through the boarding and bursting inside, and the rebels in the building collapsed at once. The accounts of the engagement since have turned on that one shot, and the artillery rather than the musketry was the arm that settled it. Beyond the weapons, the rebellion involved other equipment. The steamers United States and Charlotte of Toronto and the patrol boats of the Royal Navy were used to blockade the Niagara and the St Lawrence; on 13 November 1837 the patriots took the British battery at Windmill Hill near Prescott for a time, and when they attacked the same place again in November 1838 the British guns brought up from Kingston ended the business. That battery and the relieving artillery were the only formed heavy firepower on the British side of the border. The rebel incursions depended heavily on steamships to carry men across; in May 1838 they boarded and took the British steamer Sir Robert Peel. Those ships were at once their only means of crossing the border and their most exposed point.
tactics: 這場叛亂的戰術幾乎完全由地形、宣傳與道路決定。叛軍的準備工作做在紙上：制憲會議、宣言、傳單、公開集會，用的是報紙與政治組織的武器，真正的軍事準備則靠城北各村農民自己鍛造長矛與練習射擊；麥肯齊原本設想的計畫是一場不流血的奪權，脅持總督、逼迫議會選出行政委員，所以行軍計畫一再更改，物資與彈藥都靠志願者臨時湊集。真正開火之後，戰術就退化成一條公路上的遭遇：十二月五日，叛軍在約克城北被二十六名民兵開火即潰，說明他們沒有任何隊形與指揮控制；十二月七日政府軍以一千二百人與兩門砲沿揚奇街推進，叛軍把隊伍分在街道兩側的田地裡，卻在第一輪射擊後因誤判友軍陣亡而全面崩散。倫敦區的鄧科姆起事同樣如此，多倫多的消息傳到後，數百人未接戰即散去。英方的戰術則是三段式：先用少量民兵與義勇封鎖村鎮要道，逼迫叛軍在缺少彈藥與糧食的駐地裡作選擇；再以正規軍與民兵混合的分遣隊進行正面壓制；最後在邊境用艦隊封鎖，於一八三八年迫使海軍島的武裝與美國供應線斷開，再以炮兵解決對方在普雷斯考特的堅固砲台。叛亂者後來轉為跨境游擊，靠汽船與小艇在夜間進入島嶼與河汊奪取船隻與糧食，一八三八年五月甚至登船奪走英國汽船 Sir Robert Peel；這種夜間襲擊只延緩了結局，因為英方在同一水域有更快的蒸汽船與更嚴格的邊境緝查，麥肯齊最終在美國被捕，獵手小屋會在溫莎的失敗則把整條供應鏈切斷。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this rebellion were decided almost entirely by terrain, propaganda and roads. The rebels' preparation was done on paper: a constitutional convention, declarations, broadsides, public meetings, fought with newspapers and political organisation, while the real military preparation was left to the farmers of the townships north of the city, who forged pikes and practised their shooting on their own. Mackenzie's original plan was a bloodless seizure of power, the abduction of the Lieutenant Governor and the forcing of the assembly to elect the executive council, so the marching orders changed repeatedly and the ammunition and provisions were scraped together by the volunteers as they came. Once shots were fired the tactics degenerated into an encounter on a road: on 5 December the rebels broke before a volley from twenty-six militiamen north of York, which showed that they had neither formation nor command control; on 7 December the government column of twelve hundred men and two guns came up Yonge Street, and the rebels, posted in the fields on both sides of the road, dissolved in panic after the first salvo when they mistook their own front rank for casualties. Duncombe's rising in the London district went the same way: the news from Toronto arrived, and several hundred men dispersed without being engaged. British method ran in three stages. First, small bodies of militia and volunteers sealed the roads to the townships, forcing the rebels to choose while their ammunition and food ran out in the places where they were posted. Second, mixed detachments of regulars and militia pressed the attack in the open. Third, the border was closed by the fleet, cutting the arming on Navy Island off from its supply line in the United States during 1838, and the problem of the fortified battery at Prescott was then settled by artillery. The rebels turned afterwards to cross-border raiding, using steamers and small boats to enter islands and creeks at night to take craft and stores, and in May 1838 they boarded and seized the British steamer Sir Robert Peel. Such night incursions only postponed the end, because the British had faster steamers on the same waters and a stricter cordon along the border; Mackenzie was finally arrested in the United States, and the defeat of the Hunters' Lodges at Windsor cut the whole supply chain.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。一八三七年十二月七日蒙特哥馬利酒館之戰：政府軍出動一千二百人與兩門砲，叛軍在酒館據點的武裝人數約二百。叛軍的傷亡事件集中在前兩日：十二月四日揚奇街路障之戰中，保王派上尉羅伯特·穆迪陣亡；叛軍首領安東尼·安德森被市議員約翰·鮑威爾重傷；麥肯齊自十月起得到的消息是下加拿大叛亂已於十一月爆發，叛軍因此把行動日期從十二月七日提前。海軍島時期：麥肯齊於十二月十三日與倫塞爾瓦·范倫塞勒等二十四人先行登島，宣布成立加拿大共和國，並許諾每名志願者三百英畝土地；到十二月底約有五百名志願者聚集島上，之後范倫塞勒在返回大陸時因違反中立法被捕。一八三八年一月十三日英軍攻入海軍島，守軍潰散。獵手小屋會階段：一八三八年十一月十一日，四百人自索卡茲港登上蒸汽輪船 United States；由於指揮分歧，約翰·沃德·伯吉率二百人退往奧格登堡求援而未歸，馮·舒爾茨只帶一百五十人乘 Charlotte of Toronto 於十一月十二日抵達普雷斯考特附近的風車角；僵局至十一月十六日英軍自京斯頓調來炮兵而解除，愛國者方面一百三十七人被俘、八十人陣亡。溫莎之役（一八三八年十二月四日）：參與者在底特律以南三十英里的布雷斯特設營五六百人，真正渡海登岸的一百三十五人於凌晨兩點在溫莎以北三英里上岸，隨即被擊潰。追捕與鎮壓的數字：叛亂後上加拿大有八百餘人被捕；塞繆爾·勞恩特與彼得·馬修斯於一八三八年一月在多倫多被公開絞死，九十二人被送往范迪門地；總督海德於一八三七年年底被召回，喬治·阿瑟於一八三八年三月接任。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. At the battle of Montgomery's Tavern on 7 December 1837 the government column numbered twelve hundred men and two guns, while about two hundred rebels were armed at the tavern. The casualties of the preceding days are the better documented: on 4 December, in the fighting at the roadblock on Yonge Street, the loyalist captain Robert Moodie was shot and killed; the rebel leader Anthony Anderson was mortally wounded by the alderman John Powell; and Mackenzie had learned in October that the Lower Canada rising had begun in November, so the date of the rising was moved up from 7 December. In the Navy Island phase, Mackenzie crossed with Rensselaer van Rensselaer and two dozen others in December, proclaimed the Republic of Canada and promised each volunteer three hundred acres of land; by the end of the month some five hundred volunteers had gathered on the island, and van Rensselaer was later arrested on the mainland for violating the Neutrality Act. On 13 January 1838 the British attacked Navy Island and the garrison broke. In the Hunters' Lodge phase, on 11 November 1838 four hundred men boarded the steamer United States at Sackets Harbor; disagreements over the plan sent John Ward Birge back to Ogdensburg with two hundred men in search of reinforcements that never came, and von Schoultz reached Windmill Point near Prescott on 12 November with only a hundred and fifty men aboard the Charlotte of Toronto. The standoff ended on 16 November when British artillery arrived from Kingston; of the patriots a hundred and thirty-seven were taken prisoner and eighty were killed. In the action at Windsor on 4 December 1838, five or six hundred men had established themselves at Brest, thirty miles south of Detroit, but the hundred and thirty-five who actually crossed landed three miles north of Windsor at two in the morning and were beaten. On the suppression: more than eight hundred people were arrested in Upper Canada after the rising; Samuel Lount and Peter Matthews were publicly hanged at Toronto in January 1838, and ninety-two men were sent to Van Diemen's Land; the Lieutenant Governor Head was recalled at the end of 1837 and George Arthur took over in March 1838.
cause: 起義的原因分政治與經濟兩層。政治層是上加拿大與下加拿大都由總督任命、而非民選的立法委員所構成的寡頭結構；一八三四年改革派在議會選舉中取得多數，但「家庭公約」集團仍控制立法局，兩院僵持。一八三六年，總督弗朗西斯·邦德·海德上任後明確站在寡頭一邊：他拒絕實行責任內閣制，議會因不撥款而停擺，總督也拒絕簽署議會通過的法案；選舉中他公開支持保王派候選人，並縱容奧蘭治會社的暴力，改革派的麥肯齊與勞恩特雙雙落選。議會隨後通過了一批加重農民負債的法例，行政委員又自行設立有特權的私人銀行，進一步加深了對立。經濟層則是一八三六至三七年的歉收與歐洲金融危機：上加拿大銀行在一八三七年七月停止兌付，廣大農戶在歉收之後又面臨商人追討舊債的訴訟，一八三七年三月通過的法令更允許商人在收穫季節之前起訴，農民稍有拖延即被扣押拍賣。麥肯齊原本還指望用請願與議會辯論解決，但既然立法途徑已被堵死，剩下的選項就只有武力。外部條件同樣重要：美國政府採取睜一隻眼閉一隻眼的不干涉政策，對越境的武裝集團視而不見，紐約州北部與安大略的邊境因此成了一條可以反覆出入的走廊；而大西洋兩岸一八三〇年代的反動浪潮與歐洲的憲章運動，又把共和這個選項帶進了這些邊境小鎮的政治討論。
causeEn: The outbreak had a political layer and an economic one. Politically, in both Upper and Lower Canada the legislative councils were made up of members appointed by the Lieutenant Governor rather than elected, and the local oligarchies who dominated them controlled trade, banking and the institutions of church and state. The Reformers won a majority in the assembly in 1834, but the Family Compact still held the council and the two houses deadlocked. In 1836 the new Lieutenant Governor, Francis Bond Head, made his alignment plain: he refused responsible government, the assembly stopped granting supply, and he in turn refused to assent to the bills the assembly passed; at the elections he openly supported Tory candidates and allowed the Orange Order to use violence, and both Mackenzie and Lount lost their seats. The assembly then passed a set of laws that tightened the farmers' debts, and the executive council set up private banks with privileges of its own, deepening the quarrel. Economically, the harvests of 1836 and 1837 failed and the financial crisis in Europe spread here: the Bank of Upper Canada suspended payments in July 1837, and after the bad harvests the great body of farmers faced suits from merchants pressing old debts, with a law passed in March 1837 allowing merchants to sue before the harvest was gathered in, so that a farmer who delayed a little lost his property to the sheriff's sale. Mackenzie had hoped to settle everything by petition and debate in the assembly, but with the constitutional route blocked the only remaining option was force. The external conditions mattered too. The United States government followed a policy of non-intervention, ignoring armed bands that crossed the border, and the frontier between northern New York and Upper Canada became a corridor that could be crossed back and forth; and across the Atlantic the reaction of the 1830s and the Chartist movement in Europe had put the republican option into the political conversation of these border towns.
impact: 直接後果是殖民地政治結構的重整。兩場叛亂之後，倫敦派出考察專員達勒姆勛爵赴英屬北美調查，他在一八三九年提交的報告中指出，殖民地缺少的不是自由，而是責任內閣，並建議把上加拿大與下加拿大合併為一個省，於是一八四〇年的聯邦條例把兩地合為加拿大省，此後經一八六七年的憲法，逐步演成今日的加拿大。改革派在鎮壓之後換了策略：羅伯特·鮑德溫與拉豐丹等溫和派取代了麥肯齊式的共和主張，改以責任內閣為目標，於一八四九年落實，上加拿大從此走上通往自治邦的路。中長期的影響更落在邊境上：英國與美國在一八三八年之後的合作明顯加強，韋伯斯特－阿什伯頓條約最終解決了緬因與新布倫瑞克一帶的邊界爭議，也附帶處理了 Caroline 號事件；美國同時把注意力轉向西部與南部，維持對英國的善意。另一條長線是流放者的後果：被送往澳洲的叛亂者當中有一部分後來在悉尼的加拿大灣一帶參與建設；更特別的是，一九三七年加拿大志願兵以一八三七年叛亂領袖的名字組成麥肯齊－帕皮諾營，在西班牙內戰的國民派一方作戰，把一八三七年的旗號帶到另一個時代。
impactEn: The direct consequence was a reordering of the colonial political structure. After the two rebellions London sent Lord Durham to investigate British North America, and his report of 1839 argued that what the colonies lacked was not liberty but responsible government, and recommended that Upper and Lower Canada be joined into a single province. The Act of Union of 1840 duly created the Province of Canada, which by the Constitution Act of 1867 developed into the Canada of today. The Reformers changed their method after the suppression. Temperate figures such as Robert Baldwin and Lafontaine replaced Mackenzie's republicanism with a demand for responsible government, which was granted in 1849, and Upper Canada from then on pursued the road of a self-governing colony rather than of a republic. The longer consequences fall on the border. British and American cooperation tightened noticeably after 1838, and the Webster-Ashburton Treaty eventually settled the boundary disputes around Maine and New Brunswick and dealt, in passing, with the Caroline affair; the United States at the same time turned its attention westward and southward and kept up its posture of goodwill towards Britain. Another long line runs through the transported convicts: some of the rebels sent to Australia later took part in building the suburb of Canada Bay in Sydney; and in 1937 Canadian volunteers named themselves the Mackenzie-Papineau Battalion after the leaders of the 1837 rising and fought on the Nationalist side in the Spanish Civil War, carrying the flag of 1837 into another era.
result: 結果是叛亂在階段上被迅速壓平，但它留下的政治與地理殘局延續了數年。十二月七日蒙特哥馬利酒館的砲彈打碎了第一波起事，酒館被燒，領袖被捕，倫敦區的鄧科姆隨即在十二月中旬被平定；麥肯齊等退入海軍島宣布加拿大共和國，但只維持了約一個月，一八三八年一月十三日英軍進攻即告瓦解，麥肯齊在美國本土因違反中立法被捕。剩下的是漫長的收尾：獵手小屋會在紐約與佛蒙特一帶組織的越境襲擊從一八三八年年初延續到年底，經普雷斯考特風車堡與溫莎兩役才被徹底打斷。鎮壓的代價由雙方共同承擔：英方投入常備軍、民兵與皇家海軍的艦隊作跨境封鎖，美方則派出部隊在邊境協助。叛亂者方面，勞恩特與馬修斯被公開絞死，八十餘人被流放澳洲，被捕者超過八百人，另有大批莊園與農具在事後被保王派義勇毀掉。上加拿大總督海德被召回、喬治·阿瑟接任，一八三九年達勒姆勛爵抵達並提交報告，一八四〇年兩省合併，最終在承認英王的前提下實現了責任內閣——從此上加拿大不再尋求共和，而是尋求一個能由選民問責的政府。
resultEn: The result was that the revolt was crushed within weeks, though the political and geographical aftermath ran on for years. The shell at Montgomery's Tavern on 7 December broke the first rising; the tavern was burned, the leaders were arrested, and Duncombe's movement in the London district was put down in the middle of December. Mackenzie and the others withdrew to Navy Island and proclaimed the Republic of Canada, but that lasted only about a month: the British attacked on 13 January 1838, the island garrison broke, and Mackenzie was arrested on the American mainland for violating the Neutrality Act. What remained was a long tail. The incursions organised by the Hunters' Lodges in New York and Vermont ran from the beginning of 1838 to the end of that year and were finally broken at the battery near Prescott and at Windsor. The cost of the suppression was borne by both sides: the British committed regulars, militia and the Royal Navy's vessels to a cross-border blockade, while the United States sent forces to assist along the frontier. On the rebel side, Lount and Matthews were publicly hanged, more than eighty men were transported to Australia, over eight hundred people were arrested, and a number of farms and implements were destroyed afterwards by loyalist volunteers. Head was recalled and George Arthur took over in Upper Canada; Lord Durham arrived in 1839 and filed his report; the two provinces were united in 1840; and responsible government was finally achieved on the footing of allegiance to the Crown. From then on Upper Canada stopped seeking a republic and began seeking a government that could be held to account by its electors.
